theme: 3 terms on passing blocks of code around

terms.definition: A block of code you can store in a variable or pass to a function and run later.
terms.example: I passed a closure to the sort method so it knows how to compare two names.
terms.code:
let isShort = { (name: String) -> Bool in
    name.count < 4
}
print(isShort("Mina"))

terms.definition: A closure written after the function's parentheses instead of inside them, which makes the call easier to read.
terms.example: I used a trailing closure on map, so the code reads cleanly with no extra parentheses.

terms.definition: A list in square brackets at the start of a closure that says which outside values the closure keeps, and how it keeps them.
terms.example: I added a capture list with weak self so the closure does not keep the view controller alive.

dialogue.title: Debugging a screen that never goes away

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the settings screen never goes away. The memory graph still shows it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is it a leak? What do we have on that screen?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A timer, and it runs a closure every second.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A closure is a block of code we pass around and run later, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. And this closure uses self inside. It holds the screen alive.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I see. How do I tell the closure not to hold the screen?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Add a capture list. Write weak self in square brackets at the start.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a capture list says what the closure keeps, and how it keeps it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. With weak, the screen can close, and self becomes nil inside the closure.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. Wait, I also see sort with a long closure in parentheses. Can we clean that up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sure. Use a trailing closure. You put the closure after the parentheses.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, like map with curly braces and no extra parentheses.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. A trailing closure is easier to read, especially with one closure.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, I tried weak self in my trailing closure, but Xcode shows an error.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Check the order. The capture list comes first, inside the braces, before the word in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That was it. I put it after the parameters. Now the screen closes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Run it again and check the memory graph.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The settings screen is gone from the graph. Fixed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. A closure, a trailing closure, and a capture list. Leak fixed.
